item.title: UNC-Chapel Hill cuts all six area research centers, drawing faculty pushback
item.description: ​The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill will shutter six internationally focused academic centers as part of a broader cost-cutting initiative approved by the UNC Board of Trustees. Nathan Knuffman, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill’s chief financial officer, said the university plans to reduce $7 million in spending over the next […]

item.title: Supreme Court petitioned to decide if chilling faculty speech violates First Amendment
item.description: The request to the high court comes after the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit in October upheld the dismissal of the case.

item.title: Iranian students defy crackdown as new wave of anti-government protests launch
item.description: The protests have reportedly taken place on at least seven campuses as students demand increased political freedom.

item.title: Defense tech firm ends Cornell talk 8 minutes in after demands to cancel
item.description: At Cornell University, recruiters from a defense tech firm abruptly ended a talk after just eight minutes due to student protests.

item.title: Newsom in damage-control mode over ‘I’m like you’ low SAT remark to mostly black audience
item.description: Newsom called the criticism baseless right-wing outrage.

item.title: New York prof under review after ‘abhorrent’ remarks about black students caught on hot mic
item.description: 'I recognize these comments caused harm and pain, while that was not my intent I do truly apologize.'

item.title: U. Texas System passes ban on undisclosed ‘controversial’ material in classrooms
item.description: The University of Texas System passed a new policy Thursday requiring instructors to avoid covering controversial subjects in the classroom. “In designing course syllabi, readings, and assignments, instructors must carefully consider the topics to be covered to meet the standards of the course, exclude unrelated controversial or contested matters, clearly disclose in the syllabus the […]

item.title: TPUSA to host 1819 News CEO Bryan Dawson following death threats and student walkout
item.description: Dawson's planned appearance had prompted a walkout by several dozen students earlier in the month who said they felt unsafe with the speaker selection.
